title: DATESINPERIOD going back one month ends on the start date and excludes the same day of the month before
query: EVALUATE VAR R = DATESINPERIOD ( 'Date'[Date], DATE ( 2024, 3, 10 ), -1, MONTH ) RETURN ROW ( "Min", MINX ( R, 'Date'[Date] ), "Max", MAXX ( R, 'Date'[Date] ), "Days", COUNTROWS ( R ), "Sales", CALCULATE ( [Sales], R ) )

source.quote: The second query returns an entire month (31 days), the last day is August 15, 2008.
source.supports: the example from 2008-08-15 going back one month returns 2008-07-16 to 2008-08-15

source.quote: The result has the dates between the start date and the boundary date. The boundary date is not in the result.
source.supports: the boundary, one month back, is excluded

derivation: One month back from 2024-03-10 the boundary is 2024-02-10, which is excluded: February 11 to March 10 is 19 + 10 = 29 days. Sales: Feb 29 400 + Mar 10 500 = 900 (Feb 10 is not included).
